meta.title: Ebanist — from measurements to cut list in 10 minutes
meta.desc: Furniture design app for cabinetmakers. Design a unit on your phone and get the cut list, part labels, assembly sheet and technical drawing. Runs in the browser, works offline. Free for 1 project.
meta.ogTitle: Ebanist — from measurements to cut list in 10 minutes
meta.ogDesc: Design a unit on your phone, on site. Get the 3D model, the cut list, the labels and the assembly sheet.
hero.sub: A furniture design app for cabinetmakers. It runs in the browser — nothing to install — and keeps working offline, on site.
hero.proof: 15 furniture types · Blum & Häfele · Egger decors · PDF output
hero.alt: Two-door wardrobe with walnut fronts, 1000 × 2200 × 600 mm, drawn by Ebanist
prob.h: Three things that cost a workshop every week.
prob.1: Cut lists added up by hand, at night.
prob.1s: Every part computed from one model — finished size, to 0.1 mm.
prob.2: A wrong depth discovered on site.
prob.2s: Thickness comes from the material. If the carcass doesn’t add up, the PDF doesn’t print.
prob.3: Days lost between the drawing and the factory.
prob.3s: Cut list, labels and assembly sheet leave the same model, the same day.
story.note: Wardrobe W1000 · real data from the app

story.e.d: System 32 rows on the sides, five hinge cups per door at 100 · 579 · 1057 · 1536 · 2014 mm. The fitter reads it, doesn’t guess.

faq.q1: Do I need to install anything?
faq.a1: No. Ebanist opens in the browser and you can add it to your home screen so it opens like an app. The Android app is coming soon on Google Play.
faq.a2: Yes — in Safari on iPhone and iPad, as well as on Android phones, tablets and any PC.
faq.a3: On your device, in the browser’s storage. There is no account and nothing is uploaded. A full backup is one JSON file you can export at any time, for free.
faq.a4: Yes. After the first launch the whole app — survey, design, 3D, cut list — works without a network.
faq.a5: Any cutting service that reads a PDF or CSV cut list. The workshop package (JSON, no prices) carries every part with its edging. Native machine files (Biesse, SCM, Homag) are in development with a partner and not available yet.
faq.q6: Can I put my own logo on the PDFs?
faq.a6: Yes, with Pro: Settings → Logo on PDFs. Your company name and details go on every document.

case.meta.title: Real job: a bathroom cabinet built around the water manifold · Ebanist
case.meta.desc: 870 × 2280 mm bathroom cabinet, 16 parts, a 600 × 110 cut-out around the water manifold. Designed in Ebanist, fitted on site with zero adjustments. Site photos and app screens of the same project.
case.h: A bathroom cabinet built around the water manifold. 16 parts, zero adjustments.
case.lead: No renders. These are the photos from site and the screens of the same project in Ebanist: the numbers in the app are the numbers on the panels.
case.s1.h: The manifold stays, and the plumber must reach it.
case.s1.d: Under the sloped ceiling, in the bottom-back corner of the niche, the water manifold sticks out 110 mm from the wall, over 600 mm of height. The cabinet had to go around it, and the valves had to stay reachable.
case.c.manifold: The water manifold, before it was closed in
case.c.carcass: The carcass before the doors: central divider, shelves on the right
case.s2.h: One carcass, one depth step, one cut-out.
case.s2.d: In the app the carcass is 360 mm deep, but only 250 mm in the bottom 620 mm. The sides and the divider get a 600 × 110 cut-out in the back-bottom corner; the back is split in two and the lower part comes forward, in front of the manifold. From that, Ebanist computes every part to its finished size, and the consistency checks pass before a single document is printed.
case.c.list: Cut list: the cut-out is written on the part (✂ 600×110)
case.c.part: Side panel sheet: the cut-out to scale and its 30 holes, Minifix and dowels
case.s3.h: Every part knows where it goes.
case.s3.d: Ebanist prints a 70 × 37 mm label for every physical part: project, name, finished size, edging, number out of 16. On this job we still marked the parts by hand, on masking tape — the photo shows it as it was. The sheet next to it is the one the app prints for this project.
case.c.labels: The first 6 of the 16 labels, as the app prints them
case.c.marked: On site: masking tape, written by hand
case.s4.h: Cut, drilled and assembled from the list.
case.s4.d: The panels were cut with a track saw following the cut list, the Minifix holes drilled with the jig at the coordinates on the part sheet, and the carcass assembled on site.
case.c.cutting: Cutting a side panel to 2260 mm
case.c.step: The side panel with its 600 × 110 cut-out
case.c.minifix: Minifix holes with the drilling jig
case.s5.h: Closed, it is just four doors.
case.s5.d: Upper doors 433 × 717, lower doors 433 × 1538, three hinges on the tall ones at 100, 769 and 1438 mm. Behind the lower doors, the manifold sits behind an access hatch.
case.c.hatch: The manifold access hatch, brass ring pull
case.t.h: All 16 parts, as Ebanist gave them.
case.n.h: What the app did not do
case.n.d: Ebanist does not cut, drill or install. It gave the sizes, the cut-out, the holes and the labels; the cutting, the fitting and the knobs were done by hand, on site.
case.cta.h: Your next job, with the same numbers.
